invariants.rationale: A delivery is publishable only when the current capability gates pass.
Before GA, canonical HYDRA data uses only current schemas and carries no internal migration chain.
Release and metamodel schema versions are internal metadata, not visual identity.
External ZIP/JAR/WAR/EAR projects are inventoried recursively with bounded resource usage.
Unknown files are retained as PROJECT_RESOURCE instead of disappearing silently.
Recovered mappings expose score, confidence, fidelity, alternatives, recovered/lost fields and reasons.
Automatic selection requires high confidence and a clear score gap.
External source is preserved and failed materialization is rolled back.
Import progress uses stages and activities only; no parallel percentage callback exists.
Connection ends use sourceTerminator/targetTerminator only.
Project-backed images use PROJECT_IMAGE for all supported raster/vector formats.
OpenAPI contract and TypeScript route registry are generated from current controllers.
Frontend subsystem dependencies remain acyclic.
Production actions use shared HYDRA controls for consistent accessibility and behavior.
Visible production copy has a Spanish translation or is explicitly technical.
Caches, queues, sessions and lock registries have bounded lifecycle policies.
External tools run through bounded policies with safe arguments, timeout and output limits.
Authentication, proxy, DNS, TLS, conflict, rate-limit and storage errors preserve actionable semantics.
Complete project deletion verifies a HYDRA project root and refuses unsafe filesystem roots.
Audit storage writes one canonical compact JSON object per line and tolerates isolated corrupt lines without migration.
Frontend calls use portable backendFetch instead of hardcoded localhost URLs.
Focus, reduced motion and forced-colors behavior are centralized.
Source packaging excludes dependencies, builds, runtime data and IDE state.
The patch must reproduce the filtered target tree byte-for-byte from the declared baseline.
The release keeps Java 24 bytecode while qualification accepts supported JDK 24 or 25 plus frontend and Maven runtime gates.
API errors expose user summary, impact, safe recovery guidance, correlation evidence and separated technical detail without inventing unsafe automatic fixes.
A qualified release must survive extraction, revalidation and byte-reproducible source/SBOM regeneration.
Windows qualification resolves a complete supported JDK through provider-aware discovery instead of fixed installation paths.
Qualification checkpoints are reusable only for the same canonical source/toolchain fingerprint and keep per-stage logs.
Candidate evidence records source, SBOM, qualification, platform and effective toolchain with SHA-256 provenance.
A passing RC2 emits a machine-readable feature-freeze certificate before stable release.
